other.quote: Actions with no Frequency can be used as often as you have AP.

problem: This explains a writing convention ("a stylistic default"), not a rule. The section also opens with "Some Actions have a Frequency" and "Actions with no Frequency can be used as often as you have AP", though every card with a cost carries a Frequency.
options: Reword the opening to "Every Action has a **Frequency**, written in the title bar of its card" (dropping "Actions with no Frequency can be used as often as you have AP.") and this sentence to "An At-will Action with no roll has no Bane to take: use it as often as you can pay for it."

quote: if you are at the end of the Initiative order, use a Round Action, end your turn and a new round begins, you still can't use it again until your whole turn-cycle completes
problem: The example describes a case where nothing could happen anyway: an Action is only used on your own turn, which is when your turn-cycle ends. The difference from "once per round" shows only with a Reaction.
options: Reword: "A **Round** Action can be used once per turn-cycle, not once per round number: a Round Reaction you use late in one round can't be used again early in the next, before your own turn has started."

quote: A creature has three kinds:
problem: The table under it has four rows; the fourth (a set DC) is not something a creature has.
options: Reword: "An Action against a creature rolls against one of its three **Defenses**; some Actions roll against a set DC instead:"

quote: An EoT effect on yourself still ends at the end of the current turn.

other.quote: When an effect lasts until the end of the turn of the affected creature, it is marked **EoT**.

problem: EoT is "until the end of the turn of the affected creature". If you give yourself an EoT effect with a Reaction on another creature's turn, "the current turn" is theirs: one reader ends it then, another at the end of your own next turn.
options: Reword: "An EoT effect you gain on your own turn ends at the end of that turn; one you gain on another creature's turn lasts until the end of your next turn."
Reword: "An EoT effect on yourself ends at the end of the turn in progress, whoever's turn it is."

quote: Each position in the turn order is an **initiative slot**. Effects end at the end of an initiative slot, not of a creature.

other.quote: (the origin's own slot when it was applied on its turn, the current slot when it was applied as a Reaction or out of turn)

problem: The definition of the initiative slot stands under the heading "End of Encounter", though it is about EoT and rounds; Rounds uses the word three paragraphs before it is defined. Its last part repeats Rounds' parenthesis word for word.
options: Move it to the start of "Rounds and Durations" and cut the repeat: "Each position in the turn order is an **initiative slot**. Effects end at the end of an initiative slot, not of a creature: if a creature swaps initiative, an EoT effect still ends at the end of the slot the creature was in when the effect was applied."

quote: Each PC has their own.
problem: The chapter never says that NPCs have no Escalation (the rules log says the sentence was added here on 2026-11-25, but it is not in the text). A GM whose NPC scores a Critical can't tell from the book.
options: Reword: "Each PC has their own; NPCs have no Escalation."

quote: - **Gaining:** +1 after each encounter the party overcomes: a fight, a negotiation, a sneak, a Challenge.
problem: "Challenge" is written as a game word and has no rule. And an encounter is defined as starting when Initiative is rolled, which a negotiation or a sneak doesn't do.
options: Reword: "- **Gaining:** +1 after each encounter the party overcomes. Until scenes outside a fight have rules, the GM says which of them count (a negotiation, a sneak past a guard post)."
Reword only the word: "a fight, a negotiation, a sneak, or another challenge the GM sets"

quote: It is the only raise outside the rules above, and nothing spends Escalation.

other.quote: It is never spent: the cards that need it or grow with it read it.
it spends nothing
Nothing is spent.
and it spends nothing (see [[Escalation]])

problem: That Escalation is never spent is said five times: three times in this section, once in Chapter 1's Notation and once in Chapter 5.
options: Keep it once, in the first paragraph of Escalation ("It is never spent"), and cut the other four mentions

quote: This might feel odd for some creatures, such as a horse, but the simplification is necessary for the game to work.
problem: A sentence that defends the rule (every creature is a cube) and gives no rule.

quote: If a creature stops moving while squeezing to do another Action, meaning they don't fit completely in the space they are in, all their Rolls are Doomed and they are Vulnerable equal to half their level (rounded up) until they move to a space where they fit completely.
problem: The penalty is tied to stopping "to do another Action", but the end of the paragraph speaks of ending a turn while squeezing. One reader applies it only when the creature acts; another whenever it stands in a space where it doesn't fit.
options: Reword: "While a creature stands in a space where it doesn't fit completely and is not in the middle of a movement (it stopped there to act, or ended its turn there), all its Rolls are Doomed and it is Vulnerable equal to half its level (rounded up)."

quote: **can't enter or pass through an unwilling creature's space**

other.quote: Otherwise, passing through the squares of an unwilling creature is Difficult Terrain.

problem: Chapter 3 says an enemy's space blocks your movement. Chapter 7 (Move) still says passing through an unwilling creature's squares is Difficult Terrain.
options: Chapter 3 wins: reword Chapter 7, Move: "You can't end your movement in another creature's space, and you can't enter an unwilling creature's space at all; a willing creature's space is Difficult Terrain (see [[Movement]])."
Chapter 7 wins: an unwilling creature's space is Difficult Terrain, not a wall

quote: **A Down creature** (Dying, Shattered, Unconscious or Desperate) **and a dead one** are Difficult Terrain too, whichever side they are on.

other.quote: A creature that keeps fighting while Dying or Shattered is still a threat, and is attacked like anyone else.

problem: A Desperate creature, or a Dying or Shattered one that keeps fighting, is on its feet and attacking, yet by this line enemies walk through its square. One reader applies it as written; another only to creatures lying on the ground.
options: Reword: "**An Unconscious creature and a dead one** are Difficult Terrain too, whichever side they are on; a creature that is Down and still fighting holds its space like any other."

quote: The [[Tumble]] Action is the way past an enemy, and an Action can say otherwise (Footwork's Weave).
problem: Footwork is one of the Archer's Arts, which left the classes on 2026-11-25: no card in the book has a Weave.
options: Reword: "The [[Tumble]] Action is the way past an enemy, and an Action can say otherwise."

quote: That cone is every direction less than 45° from the straight line from you to the origin: the 45° edge is not part of it.

other.quote: That cone is every step going in a direction within 45° of the straight line from the origin to you.
or any of the 3 squares next to you after 2 steps

problem: Pushed describes its cone by the direction of each step. Read the same way here, a diagonal step is exactly 45° and never allowed when the creature stands straight in line with you, yet the example lets it end in any of the 3 squares next to you, which needs one. (The diagram could not be checked.)
options: Reword: "That cone is measured from the square the creature starts in: every square of the path must lie less than 45° off the straight line from that square to the origin (the 45° edge is not part of it)."

quote: > You hold a weapon with Reach 2.

other.quote: Weapons don't change your Reach: they have a [[Weapon Range|Range]] of their own

problem: A Reposition stays within your Reach, and Reach is your body's: the same chapter says weapons don't change your Reach, they have a Range. The example gives the Reach to a weapon.
options: Reach wins: reword to "Your Reach is 2."
A weapon's Range counts when the Reposition comes from a Weapon Action: say so in Reposition and write "You hold a weapon with Range 2."

quote: An ally's space, and a Down or dead creature's, is Difficult Terrain too; an unwilling creature's space blocks your movement (see [[Movement|Creatures in your way]]).

other.quote: **An ally's space** (any willing creature's) is [[Difficult Terrain]]: you can pass through it, never end in it, and it is the one Difficult Terrain an Evade can cross (at its double cost).
You can't Evade into or pass through Difficult Terrain, except an ally's space, which an Evade can cross at its double cost (it can't end there).

problem: The rule about creatures' spaces is written in full in Movement, again in Evade and again here.
options: Keep the full rule in Movement. Here: "Creatures' spaces: see [[Movement|Creatures in your way]]." In Evade: "You can't Evade into or pass through Difficult Terrain (an ally's space is the one exception: see [[Movement|Creatures in your way]])."

quote: **[HT]** is notation, like [W] and [Mod]: it is written in the text of the effect that creates the area, not among the Action's traits (a Basic Attack whose Tier 2 leaves caltrops is not a hazard itself).
problem: This tells the writer where to put the mark (in the text, not among the traits). A player who reads a card needs only what the mark means.
options: Reword the paragraph: "The effect declares its pattern(s) after a colon, such as **[HT: Entering]** or **[HT: Entering, Turn]**: "The area lasts 2 rounds [HT: Entering, Turn]." The three patterns are:"

quote: Most melee weapons have Range 1; a lance has Range 1 / 2.

other.quote: with Reach 2, a lance attacks at 2 / 3

problem: There is no lance in the Gear document, and no melee weapon there has a far range. The only melee weapon with a Range above 1 is the Pike (Range 3).
options: Reword: "Most melee weapons have Range 1; a Pike has Range 3." And in the next bullet: "with Reach 2, a Pike attacks at Range 4."

quote: Leaning lasts until the end of your turn, so Reactions can use it
problem: Leaning ends with your turn, so it never helps the Reactions you make on other creatures' turns, which is when most Reactions happen. "So Reactions can use it" suggests that it does.
options: Reword: "Leaning lasts until the end of your turn and ends early when you **leave your square** (any movement: an Advance, an Evade, a Forced Movement)."
Leaning lasts until the start of your next turn, so that your Reactions use it (the Lean card changes too)

quote: For example, a creature using Ground Slam (an Emanation around itself) decides whether it is affected.
problem: Ground Slam was a card of the old Bestiary; no card in the book has that name now.
options: Reword: "For example, a creature that slams the ground in an Emanation around itself decides whether it is affected."

quote: a different shape, the same 5 squares
problem: It means the same number of squares; as written it says the squares are the same, which a different shape rules out.
options: Reword: "Had you chosen right, it would start with the square diagonally southeast of you: a different shape, the same number of squares."

quote: Lantern of Faith's Bright light 3 gives Bright light in a 3 Emanation and Dim light from 4 to 6.
problem: Lantern of Faith was one of the Paladin's Arts, which left the classes on 2026-11-25.
options: Remove the sentence (the torch example before it shows the rule)
Reword: "A lantern with Bright light 3 gives Bright light in a 3 Emanation and Dim light from 4 to 6."

quote: | **Obscured** | 1 Field Bane. | 1 Field Boon, if it is Clear to you. |

other.quote: | **Hidden** | **Doomed**. | **[[Favored and Doomed Rolls\|Favored]]**. |
**You never gain this against a creature that is Hidden to you.**

problem: The row is about a creature that is Obscured to you, so "if it is Clear to you" can never be true (it should be "if you are Clear to it"). The Hidden and Unsensed rows give Favored with no condition, while the rule under the table gives it only to the creature that perceives the other better.
options: The rule under the table wins. Reword the last column: Obscured "1 Field Boon, if you are Clear to it."; Hidden "Favored, if you are Clear or Obscured to it."; Unsensed "Favored, if you are Clear or Obscured to it."

quote: Creatures in combat make noise, even standing in the same square on their turn.
problem: "Standing in the same square" can be read as "in the same square as you"; it means a creature that doesn't move.
options: Reword: "Creatures in combat make noise, even when they don't move."

quote: and your Senses are back to normal
problem: Hide doesn't change your own senses: what goes back to normal is how the other creatures perceive you.
options: Reword: "once that Action is resolved, Hide ends against every creature, and each perceives you with its own senses again."

quote: the Snake perceives her as Obscured (1 Bane on its Actions), while she only hears the Snake (Hidden: Doomed against it, and the Snake is Favored against her)

other.quote: counts as **5 Boons** or **5 Banes**, with no name: put them in with the others before cancelling

problem: The example gives the Snake 1 Bane and Favored and stops there. By Chapter 1, Favored counts as 5 Boons and the Bane cancels one: the Snake rolls normally with 4 Boons, it is not Favored.
options: Reword the end: "(Hidden: Doomed against it). The Snake gains Favored against her, which is 5 Boons: less its 1 Field Bane, it rolls normally and adds 4 (see [[Five Boons or Banes]])."

quote: Rules that count instances count them this way.
problem: No rule or card in the book counts instances of damage (Resistance, for one, is applied once per Action, not per instance), so the sentence points at nothing.

quote: Actions deal **Lethal** damage by default.

other.quote: Damage is **Lethal** unless an Action or effect says it is Nonlethal.

problem: The Damage section a few lines above already says damage is Lethal unless stated, and Chapter 7 (Nonlethal) has the rest; the first two sentences here say both again.
options: Reword the start of the paragraph: "A Nonlethal Action can deal Lethal damage by taking a Bane, and any other Action can deal Nonlethal damage by taking a Bane as well."

quote: How damage is written on a card ([V], [R], [W], [Mod] and the damage types) is in [[Roll Effects]]. Empowered, which adds a die to your damage, is in [[Chapter 8: Conditions|Conditions]].
problem: The paragraph only says where other rules are kept (they once stood in this chapter). It is a note on how the book is organised, not a rule.

quote: Dominant Damage doesn't do anything by itself, but it determines the condition you gain when you go Down. Some abilities might also make use of it.
problem: The two bullets right under it say what Dominant Damage does; "some abilities might also make use of it" promises nothing.
options: Remove these two sentences and keep "You know which Dominant Damage a creature has if you perceive them (Hidden is enough)."

quote: While **Down** (Desperate, Dying or Shattered) or **Unconscious**, you can't use Steel Yourself.

other.quote: When your total damage equals or goes above your Health Pool, you are **Down**.
(Dying, Shattered, Unconscious or Desperate)
- You can't wake up while Dying or Shattered, or while your damage is equal to or more than your Health Pool.

problem: "Down" is listed three ways: Going Down makes it any creature whose damage reaches its Health Pool (so one knocked Unconscious is Down); this line lists three states and puts Unconscious beside them; Chapter 3 lists four states with Unconscious among them, which would make a sleeping creature Down.
options: Going Down wins: Down is damage equal to or above your Health Pool, whatever state follows, and nothing lists its states. Here: "While **Down** or **Unconscious**, you can't use Steel Yourself." Chapter 3: "**A Down creature, an Unconscious one and a dead one** are Difficult Terrain too". Unconscious: remove the bullet "You can't wake up while Dying or Shattered, or while your damage is equal to or more than your Health Pool." (the bullet above it says it)

quote: Reductions from different effects add up (Judge's and Shield of Faith's), and each applies once to an Action's damage to that creature

other.quote: bonuses from different effects don't add up either

problem: Chapter 2's Stacking says effects don't add up and lists the exceptions. That damage reductions add up is an exception written only here.
options: Add a bullet to Chapter 2, Stacking: "- **Damage reductions** from different effects (see [[Guard]])."
Stacking wins: only the highest damage reduction applies

quote: It is not a Rest (see below).
problem: The warning is only needed because the sentence before it calls a Breather "10 minutes of rest".
options: Reword the paragraph: "**Taking a Breather** is a pause of 10 minutes. It removes all of your Nonlethal damage."

quote: The GM decides what is a safe place. Towns are almost always safe.
problem: The paragraph says three times that a town is safe and twice that the GM decides.
options: Reword the paragraph: "A **safe place** is a place where you are sure you can rest safely, such as a town; the wilderness, where a beast could show up at any moment, is not one. The GM decides."

quote: Each check removes Wounds of its own type only (Body Check → Body Wounds; Mind Check → Mind Wounds).
problem: The sentence before it already says "a Body Check for your Body Wounds and a Mind Check for your Mind Wounds".

quote: - Your **Speed** is lowered by 2 (to a minimum of 1).

other.quote: No effect by itself: Actions and features use them.

problem: Chapter 4 gives Bloodied and Strained effects of their own (Speed −2 and Steadiness −1; no Reaction Point regained). The Glossary says they have no effect by themselves.
options: Chapter 4 wins: reword the Glossary entry's last sentence to "Bloodied: Speed −2 (minimum 1) and Steadiness −1. Strained: you don't regain your Reaction Point. Actions and features use them too."
The Glossary wins: Bloodied and Strained do nothing by themselves

quote: > A card's Bloodied line written **after** the Tiers rewards the blow that bloodies: the Action's own damage counts. Written **above** them, it rewards finding a target already hurt.

other.quote: **Where it is written decides when it counts:** above the Tiers, the target must already be Bloodied (Strained) when the Action is used

problem: The tip restates the rule of Chapter 2, Effect Timing (where a Bloodied line is written decides when it counts) and adds the design reason.

quote: | **Tier 3** | You stabilize: roll on the Dying Table. You are no longer Dying, but you stay Unconscious. |

other.quote: | **Tier 3** | You stabilize: roll on the Shattered Table. You are no longer Shattered, but you stay Unconscious. |

problem: On the best result the creature rolls on the Dying Table again (a new Wound, as on a Tier 1), while a Tier 2 costs nothing. It is not clear whether that roll is the price of stabilizing or a copy of Tier 1's text. Shattered has the same line.
options: No roll. Reword both tables: "You stabilize: you are no longer Dying, but you stay Unconscious." (Shattered: "no longer Shattered")
The roll is meant: reword to "You stabilize, at the price of one last roll on the Dying Table. You are no longer Dying, but you stay Unconscious."

quote: When you become Shattered for the first time in an encounter, roll on the Shattered Table. Then choose to **give up** or **keep fighting**.

other.quote: When you become Dying for the first time in an encounter, roll on the Dying Table. Then choose to **collapse** or **keep fighting**.

problem: Shattered is Dying copied line for line (33 lines and three tables), with the Mind Check for the Body Check, "give up" for "collapse" and the other Table. The two copies have to be kept equal by hand.
options: Write the rules once, under Dying, and make Shattered: "Shattered works as [[Dying]], with three changes: you roll on the Shattered Table, the Check at the end of each of your turns is a Mind Check, and collapsing is called giving up."

quote: - If you take damage while Down, you roll on the Dying or Shattered Table. If you weren't Dying or Shattered yet, check your Dominant Damage first and become one of them.

other.quote: - If you take any **Lethal** damage, check your Dominant Damage and become **Dying** or **Shattered**.

problem: The bullet is in the Unconscious list but says "while Down": read alone, a Desperate creature (Down and awake) that takes Nonlethal damage would roll too, against Desperate's own rules. It also doesn't say what an NPC knocked Unconscious does when it is hit again (an NPC is never Dying or Shattered).
options: Reword: "- If you take damage while you are both Unconscious and Down, you roll on the Dying or Shattered Table. If you weren't Dying or Shattered yet, check your Dominant Damage first and become one of them. An NPC doesn't roll: [[NPCs Going Down]] decides again."
